generated.what_happened: A new study by Deep Science Ventures reveals that the nutritional value of crops, fruits, and vegetables such as wheat, apples, and carrots has declined by 20 to 50 percent over the past 60 years due to degraded soil quality and selective breeding for higher yields. Because of this decline, people today need to consume roughly double the amount of produce to receive the same levels of essential minerals like potassium, magnesium, and copper as six decades ago. Experts warn that this reduced nutrient density poses health risks, particularly for vegetarians, vegans, and an estimated five million UK adults on appetite-suppressing weight-loss drugs. To address these deficiencies, researchers advocate for rebuilding soil health and supporting farmers in adopting nature-friendly farming techniques that restore nutrient density.
